Hello my darlings. As I was lamenting news report of requests for 54" waist size for preteens(!), I remembered the 1st time I ever met a fat kid. This is a bit long but it follows on from my last post where I basically freak out about children aged 8 having a waist size that is 6.75 times their age.

I remember when I was 8 in my primary school (elementary school for some of you), I had moved from a fairly awesome open minded multi-denominational where children could call their teachers by their first names, we got to run around all the time on lunch and our principal had used to be a huge mountain adventurer beast of a dude so our day trips usually involved a lot of clambering, exploring, enjoying nature and working up a bit of an appetite. Due to living situations, for a few years I unfortunately had to move from this idyllic chilldhood environment into a horrible strict, very Catholic school - lets call it St. Andrew's - where you were forced to pray before lunch (and were screamed until you cried if you didn't), encouraged to rat on other students for minor indiscretions and where a pandemic of 'jocking' (yanking down the trousers of another child without any indication, usually on lunch break to achieve maximum humiliation, taunting and trauma) had the girls in classes being advised to stick together and avoid the 'nasty sinful boys' who were running about (no comment on the girls who also committed the same crime).

Anyway, my previous school was bit more hippy drippy and a little bit more 'posh', most of our teachers and most of our lifestyles were pretty active, fit and healthy ones. The same was not applicable to the staff and students of St. Andrew's.

I remember the first time I saw a fat child.

I was 8 and in class, I was at the 'red table' (yep, division and competition, good old psychological conditioning of 'us' vs 'them'. Get us while we're young) when I first saw him. His name was Lee. And Lee was obese. At least back then I thought he was. Nowadays he'd be referred to as 'husky' or 'stocky'. Lee wasn't stocky, he wasn't husky, Lee was a barrel shaped child composed of fat, sugar and hardened arteries. . I remember he had asthma. And I remember how he struggled to even jog after the football on our breaks. I remember Lee was a bully, always horrible to any other kid in the classroom when our teacher left us unintended (this was the 90s, kids weren't considered totally idiotic with the mentality and self presveration skills of a kamikaze lemmings back in those days), but when it came to our lunch break, Lee was a wreck. He'd jog after the football with his left hand firmly gripping his trousers. When waiting to be picked for teams, his hands were always pushed hard into his pockets, the fists bunched. He made himself as small as he could on break and 8 year old me had no idea why. He was huge. He was a beast. An ogre, a troll, this awful horrible boy who spoke only of Manchester United, his favourite sweets and boobies in 'Tekken' and inadvertently taught many of us 'colourful expressions'. Even the 10-12 year olds were intimidated by Lee's huge size and for the older kids to be afraid, us younger kids were even scared of Lee. He was fat but none of us dared say it aloud. We all knew we were thinking it, but nobody had the guts (or desire for a death wish enough) to say it first. His size was intimidating and this boy was occasionally violent. For us his fat was secondary to everything else as his behaviour was so extreme that it distracted our focus from his size and instrad of thinking "why is Lee so fat?" we were all praying "Please don't let Lee see me", but his fat afforded him a strength (or at least weight) no one could match and no one dared to ever fight back.

If you're handy with a scissors and needle and thread, get yourself some jeans closest to fitting you which have a thick double layer for the waist band. On the back, of them, where the big gap is, cut two holes on either side in the inner part of the waist band (the part that should touch your lower back/top of butt), I'd recommend spacing the holes so they're not farther out than the where the back pockets end. Grab yourself some decent elastic tape (4-6 inches max I'd imagine) from a seamstress or craft's store. Knot one end. Loop the other end in through the first hole, thread it through the gap until you can pinch it back out of the second hole. Knot this too. Stitch the knots and thread in place securely around the holes (you can cover the holes up if you're confident enough). The elastic will pull the gap in a fair bit, but won't result in the awful bunching you can get using a belt to cinch bagging waistbands in.
